messages:
rami: Heads up — we're onboarding greenlight-7b-v2 (weights from upstream). License has a clause that looks like a mix of non-commercial + no-derivatives. Question: can we quantize and serve in Dedicated, or does quantization count as a derivative?

sarah-legal: short answer: depends on the exact wording, but many ND/NComb clauses treat transformations that produce new usable weights as derivative. need to see the license text. can you paste the relevant lines? :thinking_face:

rami: sure — excerpt: "Commercial use prohibited; NoDerivatives: You may not distribute modified versions of the model weights or derivative weights in any form."

legal-bot: automated-check: FOUND_KEYWORDS [NoDerivatives, Commercial, Distribute] — risk_level: HIGH for redistribution of modified/quantized weights; medium for hosted serving (if commercial use prohibited). Recommend manual review.

anya: fwiw our quant pipeline produces a separate weight artifact (.ptq/.q4_0) — downstream can load without original FP weights. that sounds like "distribute modified weights" territory. but if we only run inference in our hosted API without giving out the quant files, is that allowed?

sarah-legal: serving via API (hosting) often isn't distribution of weights, but if the license says "commercial use prohibited" even API-based commercial access may violate it. need to confirm whether "use" includes providing inference as a paid service.

matt: for Dedicated customers the model is pinned to their GPU pools and we deliver the quantized container + weights to their VPC in some setups. that's definitely redistribution. for Redwood Hosted we never hand over weights.

jess-eng: if we can't redistribute quantized weights, could we do a "bring-your-own-weights" flow for Dedicated and only support the model on Hosted? That would avoid redistribution but hurts enterprise product.

anya: alternative: ask upstream to license us a commercial/redistrib exception (paid or free). pinging upstream is usually the fastest path. we should also run a quick eval to see if smaller open models match greenlight-7b-v2 quality — gives business options.

rami: agreed. next steps proposal: 1) legal to confirm whether "NoDerivatives" includes quantization and whether "commercial use" covers hosted inference; 2) eng to evaluate BYOW vs hosted-only product impacts; 3) reach out to upstream for a commercial/redistrib exception if needed. any additions?

sarah-legal: +1. I'll draft a short clarification email for upstream. include exact use cases: hosted API (metered commercial), Dedicated (deliver quantized weights to customer's VPC), Private on-prem (customer-run). ask for explicit permission for quantization and redistribution.

matt: I'll map product impact: feature gating on Dedicated vs Hosted, and fallback options (serve via hosted proxy, telemetry/SLAs).

anya: I'll run a quick eval baseline (latency + per-token cost) of greenlight-7b-v2 vs two alt models and post results here in ~24h. also will add a note in the onboarding checklist: if license ambiguous -> no redistribution until cleared.

rami: thanks — tagging @sarah-legal when you have the draft, will hold onboarding until we get a clear sign-off. :lock:
